- When sentiment is strongly bullish (≥0.7) and forecast is significantly above recent highs, reduce forecast by 5–10% to avoid overshoot.
- If sentiment is bearish (≤0.3) and forecast is below recent lows, increase forecast by 5–10% to avoid underestimation.
- For 30-day forecasts, if the last 3–5 days show strong upward momentum, apply a 2–3 day lag correction: subtract 1–2% per day from forecast to account for mean reversion.
- When sentiment shifts from bullish to bearish mid-horizon, reduce forecast slope by 15–25% to reflect sentiment reversal.
- If forecast peaks sharply after a spike and sentiment remains neutral or slightly bullish, apply a “cool-down” rule: cap forecast at 10% below peak for next 3–5 days.
- For 30-day forecasts with low sentiment volatility, assume mean reversion toward 30-day moving average of recent 10–15 days; adjust forecast if deviation exceeds ±15%.
